The [nineteen-base nominal checks](evidence/nominal-primitive-subtype-npm-20261014/index.json)
extend Node coverage to all nineteen primitive bases in copied records and
variants. Fields use their ordinary host representations: `undefined` (`void`
in TypeScript) for `Unit`, `boolean` for `Bool`, `bigint` for `UInt64`, `Int64`,
`Nat` and `Int`, `string` for `String` and `Char`, and `Uint8Array` for
`ByteArray`. The remaining fixed-width integers, floats and wasm32 machine
words use `number`. Each input site keeps its selected constructor and
normalization. Results project existing Lean payloads without constructor
choices, including in result-only packages.

Both author routes reproduce packages from independent source trees, install
offline and replay after relocation. The [npm CI workflow](https://github.com/seanmorris/lean-bridge/actions/workflows/nominal-primitive-subtype-npm.yml)
runs both routes and API modes and retains the original package records.
Primitive-base nominal acceptance in other hosts remains pending. Callback,
owned, recursive, dependent and broader generic Subtype combinations need
their own checks.

also cover `Unit`, `Bool`, unsigned and signed fixed-width integers, `Nat`,
`Int`, `Float32`, `Float`, `String`, `ByteArray`, `Char`, `USize` and `ISize`
in copied record and variant fields. Ordinary and reviewed full/result-only
packages pass offline installation and relocated JavaScript/strict-TypeScript
replay. Fields retain their primitive's host representation; wasm32 machine
words remain 32-bit. Input constructors retain per-site normalization, and
copied results need no input constructor. These additional primitive-base
nominal checks apply to Node; the other hosts retain the Nat coverage listed
above.

[Nineteen-base npm checks](../evidence/nominal-primitive-subtype-npm-20261014/index.json)
extend those Node fields to every admitted primitive base, including signed
and heap-backed values, floats, Unicode text and bytes. Constructors still
belong to each input site; results project existing payloads. Both author
routes and API modes pass offline installation and relocated replay with
wasm32 machine words. The other host checks below cover their tested Nat forms.

edits.previous: [Structural Subtype packages](../evidence/structural-subtype-promotion-20261011.md) have installed checks across all seventeen profiles on both source routes. [Nominal Java/Kotlin checks](../evidence/nominal-subtype-jvm-20261013.md) add those Nat forms with JDK 22.0.2 and Kotlin 2.2.0, offline installation, relocated replay and source-free deployment of both consumers on Linux x64/glibc 2.36. [Nominal native PHP checks](../evidence/nominal-subtype-php-20261013.md) add those Nat forms with PHP 8.2.33 and Composer 2.5.5, offline installation and weak/strict replay before and after relocation on Linux x64/glibc 2.36. Author/build roots are removed before installation; consumer PHP source remains required at runtime. [Nominal WIT/WASI checks](../evidence/nominal-subtype-wit-promotion-20261013.md) add the tested Nat records, variants, aliases and constructor-free results through the actual Component Model adapter and its required packaged native Lean host. Both source routes reproduce packages from two roots, install offline and replay after relocation on Linux x64/glibc 2.36 with Wasmtime 42.0.1.
